title: Data enthusiast to data expert: resources for aspiring data scientists
summary: Business executives in Africa frequently bemoan the difficulty in hiring local data science talent. And so, when we advertised for aspiring and experienced data scientists to participate in the insight2impact DataHack4FI Season 2…
body:
Business executives in Africa frequently bemoan the difficulty in hiring local data science talent. And so, when we advertised for aspiring and experienced data scientists to participate in the insight2impact [**DataHack4FI Season 2 competition**](http://datahack4fi.org), we were pleased to receive applications from over 190 people.

Across the continent, it seems young people are eager to join the **[“sexiest job of the 21st Century"](https://hbr.org/2012/10/data-scientist-the-sexiest-job-of-the-21st-century)**.

With relatively few local tertiary institutions offering dedicated data science qualifications, Africa-based data scientists tend to have varied backgrounds and many of them have either studied abroad or are self-taught in the sense that they have pieced together a range of online courses after completing an undergraduate degree. A typical data scientist might have majored in computer science, mathematics or statistics and a combination of these skills is useful.

Here are some links to courses for those looking to improve their data skills and networks for those wishing to link to other Africans with an interest in data. The list is not exhaustive, and we would love to hear recommendations on courses and networks from readers who are data scientists.

**Online courses via sites such as Coursera, edX and Udacity.** (Note that whereas several of these courses are available free of charge, there is often a cost for certification). Here are some options:

- [**Process Mining: Data Science in Action**](https://www.coursera.org/learn/process-mining ) (Coursera, intermediate level)
- **[Machine Learning](https://www.coursera.org/learn/machine-learning)** (Coursera, advanced level)
- [**Data Science Essentials**](https://www.edx.org/course/data-science-essentials-microsoft-dat203-1x-5) (edX)
- [**Microsoft’s Professional Program in Data Science**](https://www.edx.org/microsoft-professional-program-data-science) on edX
- [**DataCamp**](https://www.datacamp.com) for online learning has two tracks – **Python** and **R**. (If you are unsure which is more suitable for you, [**this article**](https://dzone.com/articles/python-vs-r) suggests some key differences between the two programming languages)
- Microsoft has an [**AI school**](https://aischool.microsoft.com/learning-paths) with a number of tutorials suitable for beginners in AI
- For a more extensive list of options see how blogger David Venturi [**ranks the data science intro courses available on the internet**](https://medium.freecodecamp.org/i-ranked-all-the-best-data-science-intro-courses-based-on-thousands-of-data-points-db5dc7e3eb8e)
- Or read crowd-sourced opinions about data science courses on [**Quora**](https://www.quora.com/What-are-the-best-data-science-MOOCs)

**(Some) formal courses at tertiary institutions.** In researching this list, it wasn't easy to identify tertiary institutions in Africa that offer a data science degree ([email me](mailto:karen@i2ifacility.org?subject=Data%20Science%20degrees%20in%20Africa) if you have details of some), although obviously many African universities offer qualifications in computer science, mathematics or statistics. Some of the options include:

- The **[African Institute of Mathematical Sciences](https://www.aims.ac.rw/)** (AIMS), which partners with universities in six African countries to offer a Master's in Mathematical Sciences (and data science and machine learning is a component of the curricula at their learning centres).
- The **[African Centre of Excellence in Data Science](http://aceds.ur.ac.rw/)** (ACE-DS) at the University of Rwanda has a number of programmes
- The [**MIT in Big Data Science**](http://www.up.ac.za/en/school-of-information-technology/article/2324622/mit-in-big-data-science-stream-c) from the University of Pretoria in South African
- The [**Master of Philosophy in Financial Technology**](http://www.aifmrm.uct.ac.za/degree-programmes/msc-data-science-specialising-financial-technology/) (which incorporates several data science components), which was launched by the University of Cape Town in 2018
- **[Master of Science in Data Analytics](https://www.kca.ac.ke/msc-data-analytics)**offered by KCA University in Kenya
- The [**AI Research Group**](http://air.ug/index.html) within the College of Computing and Information Science at Makerere University in Uganda.

**Associations, alliances and data labs.** The growing network of data-related alliances reflects shared interest in the field and it is worth having a look at the following to see whether you can participate. We have also included some labs and networks that don’t primarily or exclusively relate to the development of data-science skills, but which focus on the use of data to solve societal challenges (and therefore serve as a playground for people looking to have fun with data).

- **[Machine Intelligence Institute of Africa](http://machineintelligenceafrica.org/resources/machine-intelligence/data-science/)** (MIA) is a forum dedicated to building the machine intelligence and data science community in Africa. The website hosts an extensive list of data science resources.
- **[Data Science Africa](http://www.datascienceafrica.org)** (DSA) acts as a resource hub for data science research. A Data Science Africa event has been scheduled for November 2018 in Nigeria (Summer School on Machine Learning and Data Science).
- [**Data Science Nigeria**](http://www.datasciencenigeria.org/) is a network that facilitates mentoring of young Nigerians through face-to-face, virtual coaching classes, project-based support and holiday boot camps with a view to applying machine learning to solving social and business challenges. The theme for 2018 is big data for digital/financial inclusion.
- [**Code 4 Africa**](https://codeforafrica.org/) describes itself as “a people-driven movement that aims to empower active citizenry and strengthen civic watchdogs to help government shape and improve its services to citizens”. It emphasises open data and the analysis of available datasets for public good. According to its website, It supports "citizen labs’ in nine countries and major projects in a further 15 countries”. See whether they have something running locally.
- **[Pulse Lab Kampala](https://www.unglobalpulse.org/kampala)** is a UN innovation lab for the application of data analysis in solving developmental challenges.
- [**Tanzania Data Lab**](http://www.dlab.or.tz) (dLab) has an open working space where data can be shared and analysed for the benefit of civil society.
- [**kLab**](https://klab.rw/public/about) in Rwanda, which is another open space for IT entrepreneurs, places a strong emphasis on data through its affiliates and activities. For those who (like i2i staff) have an interest in data science as it intersects with financial sector innovation, kLab is building [**a fintech cluster**](http://disrupt-africa.com/2018/05/fintech-cluster-established-at-rwandas-klab/).

**Online data challenges (pit your skills against other to identify areas of expertise or potential improvement).**

- [**Kaggle**](https://www.kaggle.com/) is a popular site for challenges
- Keep an eye out for the launch of African data-for-good challenge platform [**Zindi**](http://www.zindi.africa/) (to be launched by Ixio Analytics).

**Online platforms act as virtual communities enabling you to find people with similar interests.**

- See the [**Awesome Data Science repository on Github**](https://github.com/bulutyazilim/awesome-datascience), which includes, for example, a list of data-science-related podcasts as well as Facebook and Twitter accounts with a data focus.
- Developer community [**Stackoverflow**](https://stackoverflow.com/) is a place where you can post your “geeky” data coding questions.
- The [**Microsoft Azure platform**](https://azure.microsoft.com) includes: open source data APIs (e.g. facial recognition)

**Other networks or virtual communities.** These include various general data-related WhatsApp groups and  Facebook developer circles or specialist groups like **[BlackinAI](https://blackinai.github.io/)**. We are really excited to launch a **[Facebook community](https://www.facebook.com/groups/DataHack4FI/)** for those share our interest in **data and tech for good in the financial sector**. We are reaching out directly to those who participated in our DataHack4FI competition but if those topics get you excited you should apply to join!
